SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Body, health & movement

lie verb

be lying down; lie down

also lie down, be lying, lying down, lie in bed, lie on the ground

classical

Sen. Ep. 87.2: culcita in terrā jacet, ego in culcitā
Liv. 21.4.7: humī jacentem

jaceō, jacēre, jacuī, jacitum

verb, second conjugation

lie, be lying (down)

Other words

  • cubō, cubāre, cubuī, cubitum — lie down, lie in bed

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cato Agr. 5.5: utī suō quisque locō cubet

    To go to bed is cubitum īre (Cato Agr. 5.5).

  • prōcumbō, prōcumbere, prōcubuī, prōcubitum — lie down, stretch out (on the ground)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Liv. 1.7.4: ipsum fessum viā prōcubuisse

  • dēcumbō, dēcumbere, dēcubuī — lie down (in bed or at table); take to one’s bed

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Plaut. Merc. 1.1.98; Suet. Ner. 48 (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • culcita in terrā jacet, ego in culcitā

    the mattress lies on the ground, and I lie on the mattressSen. Ep. 87.2

  • locō herbidō ut quiēte et pābulō laetō reficeret bovēs et ipsum fessum viā prōcubuisse

    that he lay down in a grassy spot, to rest the cattle and feed them on rich grass, being tired from the road himselfLiv. 1.7.4

  • prīmus cubitū surgat, postrēmus cubitum eat

    let him be the first to get up and the last to go to bedCato Agr. 5.5

See also sleep, bed, go to bed, sleep in, sit.

SourcesLewis & Short: jaceo · Lewis & Short: cubo · Lewis & Short: procumbo · Lewis & Short: decumbo
